blocks.text: Born in 1572 in Herakleion, Crete, he became a monk at Agarathos and studied in Venice and Padua. The Patriarchate’s account describes work in Orthodox education and opposition to the Unia.

blocks.text: He served as patriarch of Alexandria from 1601 to 1620 and then held the Constantinopolitan throne with repeated interruptions. His work included aid during an epidemic, support for printing, and an introduction to a vernacular New Testament translation.

blocks.text: The patriarchal canonization act records that Janissaries strangled him on June 27, 1638, and threw his body into the sea. It recognizes him among the Church’s hierarchs and martyrs.
